∀ n: n ∈ subtree skipped by content-visibility:auto → getComputedStyle(n).margin = auto (unresolved, not px)
∀ n: n ∈ subtree skipped by content-visibility:auto → getComputedStyle(n).margin is the used px value (the read forces the lock open); only a display:none subtree reports auto
∀ f: all rAF callbacks of frame f run before the style and layout of f, so a write in rAF is seen by the frame's own layout-time observers
∀ f: a ResizeObserver callback for a size changed in f runs in f, after layout and before the next rAF
∀ w: after the viewport becomes w the layout (media queries, vw lengths) reflects w within k = 2 rAF frames
∀ rAF callback(t): t = document.timeline.currentTime (c = 0)
a registered <number> property animated from a to b with linear timing has value a + (b − a)·p at progress p
a property registered with inherits = false and set on e reads its initial value on every child d ≠ e
classList.toggle(c, b) with (c ∈ classList ↔ b) changes nothing (no attribute mutation)
style.setProperty(k, v) with the inline value of k already v changes nothing (no attribute mutation)
getBoundingClientRect, getComputedStyle, elementFromPoint return the state after all earlier writes (forced style/layout, R4)
elementFromPoint(x, y) skips every box with pointer-events:none (AL: the allow-list equals the boxes that re-enable it)
a CSS length x lays out as ⌊64x⌋ / 64 px (LayoutUnit, 6 fractional bits, truncation)
an IntersectionObserver callback is never delivered inside the rAF callback that observes, and arrives within k = 3 frames

on a fresh load, in a 300 px grid row: a non-replaced item with a preferred aspect ratio, a definite width and height:auto (no min/max) gets its ratio height under align-self:start and fills the row under stretch; a non-replaced block item without an aspect ratio fills the row under normal (the mode table). Under normal the ratio item is engine-dependent (observed only), hence mode = other

on a fresh load, for every arm s and its used layout L, agrees(s, L): the content size respects min/max, the resolved grid-template-rows and row-gap are the used track sizes and gap, the item's row is one of them, and its measured offset and outer size are its placed box; tested on single-column grids where the start-aligned item fills its row and stretch gives the same box

a paused Web Animation with linear easing and key frames at offsets 0, o₁, …, 1 (translate or a translate() scale() transform list) has, at progress p, the piecewise linear value through the key frames (the chord of the Lean track)
translate, scale and transform animated together on one element compose as translate, then scale, then transform (right to left), each property animating independently

two nested overflow:hidden border-radius:40px boxes, the inner one composited and moved by translate, show exactly the intersection of the two rounded rectangles: the outer one cuts its own corner, the inner one cuts its own, the straight edges hold

a backdrop-filter blur child of an overflow:hidden border-radius ancestor, composited and transformed, blurs the page behind it as the same child without that ancestor does (each channel within 12 of 255 at a stripe edge)
